ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: All directors, officers, shareholders, and beneficial owners are screened against the UN Consolidated List, OFAC SDN List, EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List, and the Marshall Islands domestic AML/CFT screening database; a risk-based enhanced due diligence applies for any PEP, former PEP, or exposure to high-risk jurisdictions, with refusal of incorporation where screening results produce a positive match subject to applicable exemptions under the AML/CFT Act.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Marshall Islands Registrar of Corporations Electronic Filing System (accessible only through licensed Registered Agents; no direct public web portal for name reservation)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Statutory English-only naming; corporate names must consist exclusively of Latin script letters (A-Z), Arabic numerals, and punctuation marks commonly used in English; diacritical marks and non-Latin scripts are prohibited; the name must be in English or a romanized transliteration of a foreign word with a required English translation filed with the Registrar.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon an administrative name rejection the applicant may file a written appeal with the Registrar within 14 days of notice; the appeal must specify the reasons for reconsideration and propose a revised name if applicable; the Registrar must issue a final determination within 21 days of receipt; a failure to obtain relief at the Registrar level may be appealed to the High Court of the Marshall Islands under the Judicial Review procedures of the Civil Procedure Act.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A licensed Registered Agent must maintain a physical office in the Marshall Islands that serves as the statutory registered office; pure virtual office arrangements without a physical registered agent office are not permitted; for low-risk no-code software builders, virtual back-office operations in the agent's physical premises are permissible as long as the Registered Agent performs all statutory compliance duties.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low risk; statistically, a licensed Registered Agent's physical premises receive an unannounced inspection in approximately 5% of years under the AML/CFT supervisory framework; ad hoc on-site visits to the subscriber's claimed business site are unlikely outside a specific AML trigger or court order.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Business Corporations Act 1990, Republic of the Marshall Islands, as amended, including the provisions on incorporation, registered office and registered agent, initial directors, and officers
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Office of the Registrar of Corporations, Business Registry Division, Ministry of Finance, Republic of the Marshall Islands
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital; the Articles may authorize nominal capital, and no escrow account or bank deposit is required before incorporation
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the corporation adopt the Articles of Incorporation as filed; and that the subscriber listed in the Articles subscribe for the number of shares attributed to each, payment of consideration being deferred as permitted by law. RESOLVED FURTHER, that the registered office be established at the address maintained with the Registrar of Corporations in Majuro, and that the registered agent be retained. RESOLVED FURTHER, that the following individuals be and hereby are appointed officers: President, Secretary, and Treasurer, each to serve until the earlier of resignation, removal, or successor appointment. RESOLVED FURTHER, that corporate powers be exercised by the Board, and any officer is authorized to execute banking and licensing documents.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Business Registry Division, Office of the Registrar of Corporations, Majuro, Republic of the Marshall Islands
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit a Name Pre-clearance Application stating the proposed corporate name and intended business activity. The Registrar checks the name against the register of existing entities. A non-objectionable name may be reserved for a limited period. Business activity must not commence before the Certificate of Incorporation is issued.
required_dossiers: Registered agent name and consent, if known
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused for similarity or prohibited terminology, file an administrative objection or submit an alternative name; the Registrar re-runs the search within five business days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execution and Notarization of Articles of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notary public authorized under Marshall Islands law or consular notarization if executed outside the Republic
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the Articles of Incorporation in English specifying the corporate name, registered office address in Majuro, registered agent, authorized capital and share classes, initial directors, and lawful purpose. Each incorporator executes and acknowledges the Articles before a notary; the initial directors execute written consent to act and the registered agent executes acceptance of appointment.
required_dossiers: Articles of Incorporation, executed and notarized
Acceptance of appointment by registered agent
Subscriber identification and due diligence form
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notarial certificate is defective, re-execute the signature page before a qualified notary or RMI consular officer and resubmit the corrected document.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Filing with the Registrar and Payment of Government Fee
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Office of the Registrar of Corporations, Business Registry Division, Ministry of Finance, Majuro, Republic of the Marshall Islands
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Deliver the notarized Articles, registered agent acceptance, and any name reservation certificate to the Registrar, together with the USD 150 government filing fee. The filing may be made by courier or through an authorized filing agent. The Registrar enters the application and issues a file number or acknowledgment.
required_dossiers: Government filing fee receipt or proof of payment
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the application is queried for incomplete schedules or fee insufficiency, the applicant may cure by filing the missing item or fee balance within 30 days; if not cured, the application may need to be re-lodged.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Issue of Certificate of Incorporation and Corporate Record Book
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Office of the Registrar of Corporations, Majuro, Republic of the Marshall Islands
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After approval, the Registrar enters the company onto the public register and issues the Certificate of Incorporation. The company or its filing agent verifies the registered office, initial directors, share provisions, and effective date. Certified copies of the Articles and certificate are ordered and maintained in the corporate record book.
required_dossiers: Corporate record book and share register
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Certificate contains a typographical variance from the approved Articles, a formal correction may be requested from the Registrar without re-filing; the corrected certificate is issued after clerical review.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Adoption of Bylaws, Officer Appointment and Banking Readiness
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Initial Board of Directors acting under the Business Corporations Act
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Hold the first board meeting or execute unanimous written consents. The Board adopts bylaws, ratifies the share subscription, designates the registered office as the principal office, and appoints the President, Secretary, and Treasurer. The Board also authorizes opening a bank account, engaging the payment processors, and executing commercial contracts.
required_dossiers: Minutes or unanimous written consent of initial directors
AML/KYC package for bank and payment processor onboarding
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a financial institution requests revised board authorization, pass a supplementary board resolution correcting or supplementing the earlier approval; no registry remedy is applicable at this stage.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not applicable; the no-code website builder performs digital software services only and does not operate an industrial or manufacturing facility in the Republic of the Marshall Islands
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: No industrial operating permit required; if a physical commercial presence is later established in Majuro, the local Municipal Business License may be required

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt; office-based and cloud-software activity generates no environmental impact requiring a full EIA or environmental registration
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No industrial wastewater discharge, VOC emissions, or hazardous waste generation; electronic waste disposal must comply with EPA waste management regulations and general municipal waste rules

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: No special civil-defense permit is required for remote online operations; any leased office must maintain fire and life-safety clearance from the local fire marshal and structural occupancy approval from the building inspector where applicable

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Revenue and Taxation Division, Ministry of Finance, Republic of the Marshall Islands (Majuro, MH 96960); no integrated national income-tax e-portal exists. Corporate registration and annual filings are administered separately by the Office of the Registrar of Corporations through licensed registered agents (practical portal/account access held by the entity's RMI registered agent).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: No statutory TIN/VAT ID procurement is required for a non-resident Business Corporation ('BC'). The RMI levies no general corporate income tax, and the Business Privilege Tax ('BPT') reaches only persons that are 'engaged in business in the Republic.' A non-resident BC selling no-code web builder software exclusively to non-resident customers has no nexus, no registration form, and no TIN. If the BC later opens an RMI office, employs RMI staff, or sells locally, it must register for BPT with the Revenue and Taxation Division and obtain a BPT account number within the prescribed registration period; no other national tax registration exists.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: RMI has no check-the-box regime and no hybrid mismatch election because it has no income tax statute. The relevant statutory election is corporate-status election under the Business Corporations Act: the BC may designate itself in its articles as a 'non-resident domestic corporation' (no RMI office, assets, or business), which confirms exclusion from BPT and qualifies it for tax-exempt foreign-source treatment. Non-resident status can also be effected by filing the requisite statement with the Registrar.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: None – the RMI has no VAT, GST, or general sales and use tax. Indirect levies are limited to customs import duties, excise duties on alcohol/tobacco/fuel, and the 2% export tax on marine products. Digital services supplied by a non-resident BC to foreign customers are outside the RMI indirect tax base.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: Not applicable – no VAT/GST threshold exists. BPT registration arises only upon the commencement of business activity in RMI, without a fixed low-value exemption threshold for non-resident digital vendors; a non-resident BC with no RMI physical or sales nexus is not required to register in any local-currency amount.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: None – no e-invoicing, real-time fiscal clearance, API clearance, or digital stamping mandate applies. Stripe and Paddle payment-rail and merchant records may be retained voluntarily for corporate books, bank KYC, and OECD CRS filings, but no RMI fiscal authority clearance is required.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Not applicable – the RMI has no VAT/GST regime and therefore no 0% export rating or refund system. Digital software/SaaS exports by a non-resident BC are simply outside the RMI tax base; no zero-rating certificate, export evidence, or refund claim is required or available.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Not applicable to pure digital no-code services (no customs event); for physical goods re-export: Customs Export Declaration filed under the RMI Customs Tariff
Bill of Lading or Air Waybill (transport document evidencing despatch from RMI, where goods are involved)
Inward Remittance Certificate or bank SWIFT/payment-rail credit evidence (retained for bank and corporate compliance; RMI imposes no export-proceeds certification)
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: No clawback mechanism exists because no zero-rating refund exists. General enforcement: a misdeclared 'non-resident' BC that actually carries on business in RMI may be retroactively assessed BPT on RMI-source gross receipts with interest and late-filing/late-payment penalties; false tax or customs declarations are subject to civil fraud penalties and criminal fines/forfeiture under RMI revenue and customs law; the RMI imposes no exchange controls, so the 180-day repatriation convention reflects foreign bank/payment-rail requirements rather than an RMI statutory deadline.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: The Republic of the Marshall Islands has no domestic central bank or foreign-exchange administration; the U.S. dollar is sole legal tender under the Currency Act 1982, so monetary policy and currency conditions are effectively determined by the U.S. Federal Reserve System. Banking and financial-institution licensing, prudential supervision, and AML/CFT enforcement reside with the Office of the Banking Commissioner of the RMI Ministry of Finance, supported by the Marshall Islands Financial Intelligence Unit under the Money Laundering Control Act 2012.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The RMI maintains no exchange-control regime; both current-account and capital-account transactions are freely and fully convertible because the domestic currency is the U.S. dollar. There are no statutory restrictions on remitting dividends, interest, royalties, or service fees to non-resident shareholders and no central-bank approval is required for profit repatriation. Practical hurdles are confined to commercial-bank due diligence, correspondent-chain sanctions screening, and de-risking of remote-gaming or offshore-holding profiles; currency-transaction reporting applies at the USD 10,000 threshold.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No statutory surrender timeline, mandatory conversion ratio, or repatriation requirement applies to export receipts in the RMI. A non-resident Business Corporation may retain, allocate, and disburse SaaS subscription revenue and other export proceeds freely in USD without conversion to an authorized dealer. The only affirmative obligations are record-keeping, currency-transaction reporting, and suspicious-transaction reporting to the Financial Intelligence Unit under the Money Laundering Control Act 2012, together with any OFAC or correspondent-bank compliance procedures applicable to the USD clearing chain.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: USD Operational Account; linked Capital Escrow sub-account available
USD Operational Account; FDIC-member parent and U.S. correspondent access
Restricted development-funding account only; not a general treasury counterparty

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low-to-Medium feasibility. The RMI has no domestic EMI or digital-bank licensing regime; foreign EMI licenses are not passportable, and unlicensed deposit-taking is prohibited by the Banking Act. Global USD EMIs and neobanks generally impose enhanced due diligence or decline RMI-registered entities because of correspondent-bank de-risking. For a Low_Risk_Standard ISIC 6201 no-code website builder, the recommended architecture is to use a U.S.-chartered fintech and the Stripe Billing and Paddle collection rails for customer payments while maintaining the entity's primary treasury account at Bank of Marshall Islands.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: RMI law does not mandate in-person director attendance; the Banking Act and Money Laundering Control Act permit non-face-to-face onboarding where the bank applies enhanced CDD comprising notarized corporate documents, apostille authentication, and risk-based verification. In practice, Bank of Marshall Islands requires execution in Majuro via the registered agent or through a director's attorney-in-fact holding a notarized power of attorney; Bank of Guam accepts remote opening with video interviews of two directors and a certified corporate package. Physical appearance is therefore advisable for expedited Tier-1 onboarding but is not a statutory blocker for a low-risk software entity.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Shell-company and registered-agent dependency flag: the bank sees a non-resident Business Corporation whose only local substance is a Majuro registered agent, with no employees, office, or operational nexus.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified Articles of Incorporation and Bylaws; valid registered-agent certificate; current corporate-registry extract; Certificate of Good Standing; share register and 25%-threshold UBO schedule; board resolution appointing signatories; management representation letter; notarized board minutes evidencing substantive decisions; and audited or management financial statements of the RMI entity.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Source-of-capital red flag: initial paid-in capital or shareholder loans exceed USD 100,000 without verifiable provenance, or revenue is attributed entirely to intangible digital products.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Twelve-month bank statements of every shareholder or funding provider; executed subscription agreements and loan agreements with commercial terms; source-of-wealth questionnaires; tax returns or dividend distribution records in the shareholder's jurisdiction; Stripe/Paddle settlement reports and invoices evidencing genuine SaaS or visual-template revenue; and a memorandum explaining intercompany transactions with confirmation of no round-tripping.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: RMI negative-news nexus: automated reputational screening associates the jurisdiction with remote gaming, crypto casinos, and flag-of-convenience structures, elevating the underwriting risk rating.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Business plan mapped to ISIC 6201 and NAICS 511210; live or staged demonstration sites of the no-code website builder; domain registration and trademark certificates; commercial customer contracts and data-processing agreements; a statement confirming no gaming, gambling, or cryptocurrency acceptance; and professional references plus a visible digital footprint including product listings and developer profiles.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctions or PEP name-matching hits: a director or beneficial owner perfectly or partially matches an OFAC, EU, or UN listing, or is a PEP in a high-corruption-index jurisdiction.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified passport or national-identity document; vendor PEP/sanctions screening output showing confidence threshold and matched-alias analysis; explanatory affidavit for homonyms; birth or nationality certificate; evidence that no sanctioned party directly or indirectly controls the entity; good-conduct certificates from the state of residence; and a signed declaration confirming no dealings with OFAC-embargoed territories.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Payment-rail underwriting block: Stripe Billing or Paddle classifies the no-code website builder as a digital-goods or website-design merchant with a high refund or chargeback profile and imposes rolling reserves or termination thresholds.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Merchant underwriting pack including a product demonstration, published terms of service, refund and cancellation policy, domain age and DNS reputation report, server-region evidence, reproducible low-code builder screenshots, and a twelve-month revenue forecast; third-party URL reputation reports; and records of prior merchant-account standing at other processors as objective evidence of chargeback history.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Capital injections must be remitted in USD as SWIFT MT103, or Fedwire/CHIPS where funds originate from the United States, to the beneficiary BIC or ABA routing number of the RMI account at Bank of Marshall Islands or Bank of Guam. The remittance must reference the subscription, loan, or share-capital agreement and carry an internationally recognized ISO 20022 purpose code such as EQUI for equity contributions, LOAN for intercompany loans, ROYA for royalties and software license fees, or CCFT for cost-fee transfers. The RMI prescribes no statutory purpose-code table or exchange-control pre-notification; however, aggregate inflows of USD 10,000 or more require currency-transaction reporting to the Financial Intelligence Unit, and inflows above USD 250,000 trigger enhanced source-of-funds verification by the receiving bank. To avoid recharacterization of hidden equity, all capital must be documented either as paid-in shares evidenced by a subscription agreement and board minutes, or as arm's-length shareholder loans evidenced by a notarized loan agreement with repayment schedule, interest terms, and intercompany transfer-pricing documentation.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound treasury payments are cleared through (i) SWIFT MT103 for supplier, payroll, hosting, and marketing disbursements, with the RMI bank instructing its U.S. correspondent for Fedwire or CHIPS settlement; (ii) SWIFT MT202/COV for correspondent-chain liquidity transfers and same-day cover payments; (iii) commercial documentary credits under SWIFT MT700/MT707 and ICC UCP 600 for procurement of infrastructure, software development capacity, or equipment requiring bank-guaranteed settlement; and (iv) Stripe Billing and Paddle for card-network clearing of customer refunds, chargebacks, and subscription-billing adjustments into and out of the USD account. All outbound wires are screened by the correspondent chain against OFAC and other sanctions regimes; no central-bank approval is required, but the bank files applicable Currency Transaction Reports and Suspicious Transaction Reports at the statutory thresholds.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: No in-RMI FX market exists, so hedging is permissible only through the parent treasury, a licensed U.S. broker-dealer, or a non-resident bank, and must be supported by the RMI entity's documented balance-sheet or committed cash-flow exposure.
Deliverable forward currency contracts for EUR/USD, GBP/USD, and AUD/USD covering settled invoices and committed disbursements.
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) for currencies with restricted convertibility or limited USD clearing access, cash-settled in USD upon fixing.
Cross-currency interest-rate swaps and currency swaps documented under an ISDA 2002 Master Agreement with a swap dealer and executed Credit Support Annex.
OTC and listed FX options, including puts, calls, and zero-cost collars, for hedging subscription-revenue volatility and prospective liquidity events.
FX swap and tom-next liquidity lines with the correspondent bank where same-day funding mismatches arise from Paddle or Stripe settlement cycles.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Corporate Report and accompanying annual franchise tax remittance
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registrar of Corporations, Office of the Attorney General, Marshall Islands
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before the last day of the calendar month containing the incorporation anniversary; e.g., a certificate issued on 15 March is due by 31 March annually.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing triggers a surcharge on unpaid franchise tax and a late-filing penalty; continued non-compliance for two consecutive years may result in administrative strike-off or dissolution of the Business Corporation after formal notice.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No compulsory independent audit applies to a standard non-resident Business Corporation solely on revenue or asset thresholds. An audit becomes compulsory only for licensed banking, insurance, or trust activities, when requested by the Registrar, or when a shareholder holding 5% or more of the issued shares demands an audit.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Marshall Islands law does not mandate IFRS or a specific local GAAP. Books and records must accurately reflect transactions and financial position; IFRS and US GAAP are commonly accepted frameworks for any voluntarily prepared audited statements.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: No annual UBO return is filed with the Registrar. However, the company must confirm annually to its registered agent the current beneficial owners, shareholders, directors, officers, and registered office details. Share transfers must be recorded promptly in the Register of Members, and the registered agent must maintain updated UBO data under the anti-money laundering regulations for inspection by the Registrar or competent authorities upon request.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: $400–$800 per annum depending on service provider and compliance workload
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: $3,000–$8,000 per engagement when an audit is voluntarily required by shareholders, banks, or counterparties

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 0% for a non-resident Business Corporation (BC); the Marshall Islands Income Tax Act imposes no corporate income tax on foreign-source income and the entity operates under a tax-exempt zone classification.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Full statutory exemption: no corporate income tax, no capital gains tax, no withholding tax on dividends/interest/royalties, no sales tax or VAT. The only recurring fiscal charges are fixed government fees, principally the annual report fee (USD 200–500 depending on authorized capital) and a business license fee only if domestic-source activity is conducted.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: No income tax return is required for a tax-exempt non-resident BC. The sole recurring statutory filing is the Annual Report under the Business Corporations Act 1990, submitted by a licensed registered agent through the Marshall Islands Online Corporate Registry (e-Registry) administered by the Office of the Registrar / International Registries (Marshall Islands) Inc.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual (on the calendar anniversary of incorporation).
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Filing is due on or before the anniversary date of incorporation each year; an extension period may be granted by the Registered Agent within the anniversary month. A Certificate of Good Standing is issued only after the annual report and fee are accepted.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Line 1 — Corporate Name and File Number
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Registered legal name of the BC and its unique Marshall Islands file number.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident BC: verify exact English corporate name; no local language translation required.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Line 2 — Registered Agent and Registered Office
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Name and physical address of the licensed Marshall Islands registered agent and registered office in Majuro.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Agent must be a licensed RMI corporate service provider; a post office box alone is insufficient, but a certified mail forwarding address is accepted.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Full legal names, nationalities, and residential addresses of all directors (and secretary, if appointed).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident directors are permitted; there is no local residency or nationality quota, but a natural person must be named.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Line 4 — Authorized and Issued Share Capital
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Amount of authorized share capital, class of shares, and number of issued shares.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: No minimum capital requirement is imposed; a non-resident BC may declare non-assessed or no-par shares.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Confidential beneficial ownership information identifying each natural person holding 25% or more of shares or control.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident ultimate owners must be disclosed to the agent and Registrar under the AML framework; the schedule is not publicly accessible.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Line 6 — Officer Declaration and Tax-Exempt Status
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Certification by a director or agent that the company has not derived income from sources within the Marshall Islands and continues to qualify for tax-exempt offshore status.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident BC must confirm no domestic-source income and no physical place of business in RMI territory; misdeclaration triggers penalties.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing attracts an administrative penalty of USD 100 plus USD 5 per day of continued default (statutorily capped at USD 500 per annual report); persistent non-filing results in administrative dissolution, loss of good standing, blocking of a Certificate of Good Standing, and payment of reinstatement fees before any notarization or bank onboarding can resume.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 0% — the Marshall Islands imposes no dividend withholding tax on distributions made by a Business Corporation to its shareholders, regardless of shareholder residence.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: The Marshall Islands has no comprehensive double taxation agreement network relevant to a non-resident BC and does not routinely issue formal Tax Residency Certificates (TRCs). Treaty relief is therefore not required for outbound repatriation because the domestic statutory exemption fully eliminates RMI-source withholding. Where an investor-side credit is nevertheless sought, the practical protocol is: (i) obtain a Certificate of Good Standing and certified Articles of Incorporation from the Registrar; (ii) have the registered agent issue a certified status letter confirming the tax-exempt offshore classification; and (iii) where the shareholder jurisdiction maintains a limited arrangement with the RMI (e.g., TIEA or Compact context with the United States), file the certificate bundle and a treaty-benefit self-declaration through the recipient's local tax authority.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory rate 0% on outbound royalties and debt interest; no domestic withholding tax articles exist. Treaty rates are not applicable in practice due to the absence of comprehensive DTAs; all cross-border payments remain subject solely to AML/sanctions screening and bank-level source-of-funds documentation.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Not applicable — no corporate income tax base exists for a non-resident BC, therefore no arm's length adjustment regime, Local File, or Master File documentation obligation is triggered; the effective threshold is USD 0 (no TP statute).
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Applicable — the Economic Substance Regulations 2020 (enacted under the Economic Substance (Implementation) Act) require International Companies and, in defined cases, Business Corporations conducting 'relevant activities' to demonstrate adequate substance in the Marshall Islands: board meetings and management in Majuro, local books and records, and sufficient employees and expenditure proportionate to the activity. The target no-code website builder (ISIC 6201) must be specifically assessed against the 'intellectual property business' category: if the platform derives royalty or licensing income held in the RMI, full ESR reporting and the CIGAR (Core Income Generating Activities) return are mandatory. If the BC merely holds equity interests in an operating subsidiary and earns only dividends and capital gains, it qualifies for the passive pure-equity-holding exemption and is excused from active substance. A failure to file ESR annual returns is treated as a separate registrable offense.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax Evasion and Unlicensed Domestic Business
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: A tax-exempt non-resident BC derives income from sources within the Marshall Islands (e.g., physical marketing office, local employees, or on-island software delivery) without registering under the Income Tax Act and without obtaining a business license.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Retroactive assessment of domestic corporate income tax at the applicable Income Tax Act rates, plus interest and penalties for underpayment; business license fines of up to USD 5,000; the Registrar may strike the company off the register and revoke the Certificate of Good Standing.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and officers may be held personally liable for taxes withheld or assessed where they knowingly authorized domestic trading without license; civil restitution of improperly distributed dividends; criminal prosecution for making false declarations carries fines and imprisonment.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operation of a relevant activity — such as high-value IP exploitation by the no-code website builder earning licensing or royalty revenue — without adequate physical presence, employees, or expenditure in the Marshall Islands, and failure to file ESR annual returns and CIGAR declarations.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Initial financial penalty up to USD 10,000; continued default attracts additional penalties up to USD 20,000; the Registrar may replace or remove the registered agent, and the company may be struck off the register.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who knowingly authorize false ESR declarations are subject to personal fines and disqualification from acting as directors for up to 5 years; the High Court may impose travel bans and asset-protection orders pending investigation of cross-border substance arbitrage.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Money Laundering and Shell Company Abuse (AML)
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Use of the BC as an anonymous invoicing or payment conduit for third-party funds, absence of customer due diligence under the Anti-Money Laundering and Counter Financing of Terrorism Act 2012, or failure to file and update the confidential Beneficial Ownership schedule.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Corporate fines up to USD 500,000; criminal liability for natural persons with imprisonment up to 15 years; asset freezing and civil asset forfeiture orders; international mutual legal assistance proceedings may be initiated by foreign tax authorities.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and compliance officers are personally criminally liable for conspiracy and knowingly permitting the laundering of proceeds; the High Court may issue travel bans and exit restrictions pending extradition or mutual assistance; conviction results in mandatory imprisonment.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Fraudulent Trading and Misrepresentation to Creditors
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Issuing shares with fabricated paid-up capital, paying phantom dividends to non-resident shareholders while insolvent, or continuing to trade with intent to defraud creditors of the software subscription business.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Judicial winding-up, civil restitution orders in favor of creditors; penalties under the Business Corporations Act for false statutory declarations of up to USD 5,000 per offense; disqualification of directors from managing any RMI corporate entity.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The corporate veil is pierced: directors are liable without limitation for fraudulent trading; the High Court may issue arrest warrants and travel bans, impose asset-protection orders, and on conviction directors face imprisonment of up to 5 years.
